channel.title: Carat Capital — The Trade Paper of the Jewelry World
channel.description: Prices, intelligence and analysis from every desk of the stone trade: diamonds, gold and metals, gemstones, watches, auctions, retail and technology.

item.title: India's gold imports fall 45% to US$2.3bn as ETFs reach 121.3t
item.description: Domestic prices traded below import parity through August, and discounts widened from US$34 an ounce in July to US$51. Indian gold ETFs took INR25.97bn, an inflow up 67% on the month.

item.title: RAPI restates all five daily points read a day earlier
item.description: The one-carat series read on 21 September and again on 22 September differs at every overlapping date, by between 12 and 27 cents. The level is barely changed; the dating of a quote is not.

item.title: Thailand's gold exports fall 59.22% in July to US$411.04m
item.description: Gem and jewellery exports excluding gold slipped 6.36% to US$737.93m, the first monthly fall after four straight gains. Seven-month exports excluding gold still run 9.87% ahead at US$8,981.12m.

item.title: Gold falls $14.50 to $4,333.70 with all four metals lower
item.description: Silver gave up 0.92% and palladium 0.78% against Monday's marks on Kitco's bid. Gold's overnight range ran from $4,290.70 to $4,376.90, a span of $86.20.

item.title: RAPI's 1-carat rises to $3,916.19 across five sessions
item.description: The index published a new point on each of 17, 18, 19 and 20 September, a rise of $4.28 from the 16th. IDEX's broad one-carat driver averaged $3,051.17 on the same morning, 22.1% below the narrow benchmark.

item.title: De Beers and Shanghai's bourse meet on natural-diamond value
item.description: The Natural Diamond Council and the Diamond Federation of Hong Kong convened the session on 17 September, during Jewellery & Gem World. The World Federation of Diamond Bourses and De Beers sat on the panel; no figures were released.

item.title: Gold opens the week $28.80 lower at $4,348.20 an ounce
item.description: Silver added half a cent, platinum lost a dollar and palladium lost a dollar. The board's overnight range on gold ran from $4,339.30 to $4,384.30, a swing of $45.

item.title: Rings.com puts the lab-grown 1-carat median back at $571
item.description: The September edition read 251,098 listings at seven US retailers on 17 September. Ritani raised its one-carat asking median 26% while Brilliant Earth cut its 1.5-carat cell 32%.

item.title: ICBC sets gold margin at 190%, forced-sale line at 170%
item.description: More than 10 Chinese banks have shut or tightened personal access to Shanghai Gold Exchange metals trading this year. The count stood at 6 on 9 September; Pudong Development closes its channel on 25 September.

item.title: 300kg of gold clears Sanya airport from Singapore
item.description: The consignment transited Guangzhou and moved into the Shanghai Gold Exchange's Sanya warehouse. Customs ran advance declaration, air-to-air transit and apron collection as one procedure, which Sanya Daily reports as a first at the port.

item.title: DGFT drops the RCMC requirement on exports under ₹3 lakh
item.description: Notification 36/2026-27 amends paragraph 2.57 of the Foreign Trade Policy 2023, effective 15 September. Consignments up to USD 3,000 were 43% of India's shipping bills and 0.86% of export value from 2021-22 to 2025-26.

item.title: India's polished exports fall 4.93% in value, rise 3.23% in carats
item.description: Total gem and jewellery exports reached $2.30 billion in August, up 3.14% year on year on the council's figures. Studded gold jewellery added 51.22% to $642.85 million.

item.title: DGCX hands its trading and clearing engine to TCS
item.description: Tata Consultancy Services will supply BaNCS for central counterparty clearing and trading, and Quartz for surveillance and connectivity. TCS shares rose 5.19% to ₹2,315 on the National Stock Exchange on 15 September.

item.title: SCS retires SCS-007, the gemstone standard no miner adopted
item.description: The scheme covered natural and laboratory-grown diamonds, emeralds, rubies and sapphires, and ended on 1 September. Companies already certified may use their certificates until expiry, but SCS will no longer audit or maintain the standard.

item.title: Silver fixes at $67.035 in London, highest since 28 August
item.description: Kitco's Friday close put spot silver at $66.127, down 1.06% on the session and 1.35% below the London fix. Gold's fix eased to $4,348.15 and palladium's rose to $1,315.50.

item.title: Noonans lists two medieval gold rings at £9,000 to £13,000
item.description: Andrew Riley found both with a metal detector in fields near Northallerton in 2024, four months apart. The Blood of Christ ring carries £5,000 to £7,000 and the St Margaret ring £4,000 to £6,000.

item.title: Botswana's Gaolathe ties lab-grown's rise to De Beers doubt
item.description: At Chatham House on 17 September, the vice president said uncertainty over the partnership weakened confidence in natural stones. Anglo American is selling its 85% stake and Botswana holds the other 15%.

item.title: Watches and Wonders adds 9 brands to its 2027 roster
item.description: Thirteen new exhibitors are now confirmed for the salon, which runs 5 to 11 April. Porsche Design, Berneron and Fortis are among nine named on 18 September, alongside four announced in June.

item.title: Sotheby's sells HK$267.5m in Hong Kong as rubies take top three
item.description: A Mauboussin ruby necklace led at HK$16 million, 1.45 times its high estimate. Cartier tutti frutti earrings made HK$7.9 million on an HK$850,000 high estimate, and over 180 lots were offered.

item.title: Silver adds 4.87% to $66.835, highest mark since 31 August
item.description: Gold added $65.00 to $4,375.70, platinum $38.00 to $1,807.00 and palladium $35.00 to $1,305.00, all read off Kitco's bid at 06:03 EDT. LBMA's Thursday fixes confirm the direction on every metal.

item.title: Patek Philippe split-seconds carries CHF 4m estimate at Phillips
item.description: The 1945 chronograph heads Phillips' Geneva Watch Auction XXIV on 7 and 8 November, a sale of more than 200 lots. An F.P. Journe carries CHF 1m to CHF 2m and a Paul Newman Daytona CHF 1.6m.

item.title: Stuller puts jewellery stores at 26% of doors, 48% of dollars
item.description: Harold Dupuy of Stuller told the American Gem Society's Conclave that jewellery is taking share from big-box stores. The presentation published neither a period nor a denominator for the two shares.

item.title: GJEPC takes 89 Indian companies into 1,228 sq m in Hong Kong
item.description: The India Pavilion opened in two phases, at AsiaWorld-Expo on 14 September and the Hong Kong Convention and Exhibition Centre on 16 September. Exhibitors at the fair come from 44 countries.

item.title: Shanghai Diamond Exchange signs Beijing pact with three governments
item.description: Botswana, Namibia and South Africa signed alongside the exchange in Beijing on 15 September. De Beers chief executive Al Cook witnessed it, and eight Chinese retail brands attended without signing.

item.title: Hong Kong sets Q1 2027 for central gold clearing
item.description: Hong Kong's Policy Address, delivered 16 September, also has the HKMA weighing a larger Exchange Fund gold holding. The HKEX will detail renminbi-denominated, physically settled gold futures this year.

item.title: Swiss watch exports rise 9.1% in August, US shipments fall 19.4%
item.description: The FH put August shipments at CHF 1,789.2m, with one more working day than 2025. The United Kingdom rose 46.1% and France 113.5%, while the United States stayed the largest market.

item.title: US luxury store openings fall 46% to 123,334 square feet
item.description: JLL's 8 September leasing report counts the first half of 2026 against 227,000 square feet a year earlier. Jewellery and watch retailers took 43.5% of the smallest size band.

item.title: India raises gold hallmarking fee to Rs 75 an article
item.description: The gazette notification of 14 September also sets a Rs 200 minimum per consignment and leaves silver at Rs 35. Indian outlets put the previous gold rate at Rs 45.

item.title: Victorins lists over 250 lots for its 20 September sale
item.description: The Fredericksburg, Virginia house carries a Cartier Libre Noeud diamond watch at $52,500 to $105,750. A Patek Philippe Calatrava carries $27,000 to $53,850, both the house's own estimates.

item.title: Star Diamond names Jean Raymond Boulle II chief from 1 October
item.description: He succeeds Lester Kemp, interim chief executive since November 2025, at the company's Fort à la Corne kimberlite diamond project. Rapaport reported the appointment on 15 September.
